summary: Deploy delegated Slack channel claim flow with automated external-collab guards and Confluence sync
description: Issue summary: We need a delegated channel-claim workflow in Slack that allows pod leads to claim ownership of unclaimed channels, ties channel metadata to a Confluence project page, and enforces automated guards for external collaborators. Impact: Without this flow, stale channels remain unowned, external invites bypass review, and auditability is weak for compliance. Request: Implement a Slack provisioning flow + bot command /claim-channel that triggers a lightweight approval (pod lead or delegated approver), writes metadata to a Confluence template page, and applies channel-level restrictions for external guests until an approval is recorded. Background: Several pods requested a streamlined way to take ownership of legacy channels created by experiments. Security flagged a recurring gap where external guests were occasionally added to channels without a documented justification. The proposed flow reduces manual ticket churn and centralizes audit artifacts.
request_flow: 1) User runs /claim-channel in a channel. 2) Bot posts ephemeral form: proposed owner, purpose, retention window, external-collab needed (yes/no), linked Confluence doc title. 3) If external-collab=yes, bot requires a delegated approver to ACK; if no approver available, channel is marked 'quarantine' (restricted posting) and Ops notified. 4) On approval, bot sets channel topic with standardized metadata stub and creates a Confluence page from the 'Channel Owner' template with links and retention policy. 5) Channel ownership is recorded in the centralized Jira space for operations reference.
acceptance_criteria: /claim-channel slash command deploys to prod and accepts owner, purpose, external-collab flag, and Confluence title
Bot posts approval request to designated approver group and enforces 48h TTL for approvals
Channels requiring external access are put into restricted mode until approval is completed
Successful creation or update of a Confluence page from the 'Channel Owner' template with a permal link
Record created in the internal Jira operations tracker with link back to Confluence and slack channel
Audit log entries emitted to the central audit export pipeline for every claim action
steps_for_ops: Provision Slack app scopes: commands, channels:write, users:read, chat:write:bot, admin.conversations:write (if available)
Add new approver group 'channel-claims-approvers' and seed with pod leads
Create Confluence template 'Channel Owner' in /spaces/OPS/Pages and grant bot account edit rights
Deploy Lambda (or internal function) to handle slash command and approvals; wire to existing audit export webhook
Run rollout in canary org unit (research-pods) for 48 hours, collect metrics on claims and quarantines
If metrics stable, schedule org-wide rollout and add to on-call rotations for support
